grades.quote: Mac OS X is a UNIX system and so needs to support files with multiple names (created with `link` ) or no names (if still in use when unlinked).
grades.reason: Only touches the topic. It notes that a POSIX file can have no names if it is still in use when unlinked, and describes how HFS Plus handles that case. It does not explain why the file stays readable.

grades.quote: A reference count tracks the number of references to a particular open file.
grades.reason: Gives background for the mechanism: open files are reference-counted, and the inode is released only when the count reaches zero. It never mentions unlink or links, so it does not directly explain the behavior.
A list of exercises. It does not explain why a file stays readable after unlink.

grades.quote: When that count reaches zero and the file is not in use by any process, the operating system deletes the file. The operation users normally think of as deleting a file actually just removes a name; the underlying file may or may not be deleted as a consequence.
grades.reason: Directly explains the cause. Unlink only removes a name and decrements the inode's link count. The file is deleted only when the count is zero and no process is using it. A process that still has the file open can therefore keep reading it.
